canonical.title: Detect Cycle in a Directed Graph
canonical.sourceFilePath: 13. Graphs/2. Traversal Problems/12. Detect Cycle in Directed Graph.cpp

narrative.title: The Circular Approval Chain Alert
narrative.scenario: A workflow engine routes approval requests along one-way dependency edges between stages. A stage that must wait on a chain that eventually waits back on itself deadlocks the pipeline. The engine needs a one-shot audit: does the one-way dependency map contain any loop, no matter how deeply buried?
narrative.inputFormat: An integer v (stages numbered 0..v-1) and an edge list edges where each entry [u, w] is a one-way dependency u -> w.
narrative.outputFormat: Return true if the directed graph contains a cycle, otherwise false.

testCases.explanation: 0 -> 1 -> 2 -> 0 is a closed loop of approvals.
A straight dependency chain never loops back.

hintLevels: Level 1: In a directed graph, a visited node is not enough — only a node on the CURRENT path closes a loop.
Level 2: Keep two marks: globally visited, and on-the-current-recursion-stack; un-mark when a branch finishes.
Level 3: Meeting a node that is on the stack is the cycle signal; meeting a finished node is harmless history.
